basis: Core syndrome combines severe intellectual disability, skeletal dysplasia with short stature, and nephrotic renal disease.
Papillary tumour arising from the CNS meninges.
Factor IX deficiency defines a coagulation disorder; common destructive arthropathy is not established for this severity.
Isolated developmental abnormalities of the eye: microphthalmia and coloboma.
Postinfectious vascular inflammation; glomerulonephritis and mononeuropathy each 30-79%. Cutaneous vasculitis also 30-79%, omitted under cap in favour of renal and nerve damage.
Neoplasm arising in the anal canal or margin; lymphoma is only one subtype.
Congenital enlargement of the tongue, an oral structure; other listed organ abnormalities occur in only 1-4%.
Immune-mediated small-vessel inflammation with characteristic cutaneous disease; internal-organ damage is not common across the umbrella.
Primary ovarian endocrine failure with hypergonadotropic hypogonadism and delayed puberty in 2/2 patients.
Defined hepatobiliary injury from CFTR dysfunction; other manifestations of cystic fibrosis are outside this liver-specific concept.
Skeletal dysplasia and hormone resistance define disease. Developmental delay 2/2; hearing impairment 1/2. Renal agenesis 1/3 omitted under cap; estimates use small samples.
Bone necrosis defines the disease; suspected nitrogen embolism does not establish a separate vascular disorder.
Dicrocoelium liver flukes infect and occupy the biliary tract.
Inflammation confined to the tendon paratenon; inflammation alone does not establish an immune-mediated mechanism.
Lysosomal sphingolipid disorder with CNS and peripheral demyelination. Progressive optic atrophy and visual loss commonly exceed 30%; auditory brainstem delays are neurologic.
Isolated eyelid disorder with recurrent swelling leading to eyelid tissue atrophy and laxity.
Bone fragility defines OI type I. Hearing loss affects roughly 30-50% over adulthood; blue sclerae do not impair function, and dentinogenesis imperfecta is only 5-29%.
Defined by global developmental delay or intellectual disability with autism and behavioural abnormalities.
Meningeal tumour of the diaphragma sellae; optic apparatus compression causes visual impairment in most clinical series (>30%). Pituitary dysfunction is less consistent.
Defined as viral or bacterial infection of the testes; reproductive location has no axis, and common endocrine failure is not established.
Defined by azoospermia and male infertility. One low-testosterone measurement does not establish persistent endocrine dysfunction across this disorder.
Placental trophoblastic disease has no axis. Bleeding-related anemia is secondary to reproductive hemorrhage; hyperthyroidism occurs in only 5-29%.
Viral infection directly affecting ocular structures, including conjunctiva, cornea, iris, retina or eyelids.
Invasive nematode infection; cutaneous/subcutaneous larval migration with tissue inflammation occurs in most cases (>30%). Neurologic and pulmonary invasion are minority forms.
Presynaptic neuromuscular junction disorder; fixed knee contractures 4/7 and scoliosis 3/7 support skeletal involvement. Ocular weakness reflects NMJ dysfunction; respiratory weakness 2/7.
